messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED • INF-482 • embeddings-downstream — Tokenization throughput dropped >70% in us-east-1, increasing queue latency and OOM spikes on model-worker-42. Severity P1. Paging joel_oncall and eng-sre.

joel_oncall: on it. just saw the paging. pulling up dashboards now. any initial RCA hints? :eyes:

mike_sre: looking at runtime logs — we have repeated kvstore timeouts and a surge of long tail requests pinned to seq_len ~8k. seems correlated with a customer batch job hitting embeddings endpoint.

anita_prod: customer-signal: We got an alert from AcmeCorp reporting timeouts for embeddings calls. They say it started ~15m ago. Raising priority with their TAM.

joel_oncall: thanks. mitigating now — adding temporary rate-limit on embeddings route for non-premium keys to reduce load. applying policy.

sara_platform: rolled a canary of a config change to gateway to enforce per-key qps cap. policy: "embeddings.qps.default=10". command:
```
curl -X POST https://console.api/ratelimit/apply -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings","policy":"per_key:10"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

ops-bot: ratelimit change deployed to 6/8 gateway nodes (canary). Monitoring metrics: token_throughput +2% after change.

mike_sre: kvstore timeouts still happening but queue depth reduced ~30%. I’m going to restart model-worker-42 to clear bad cache. will coord with joel.

joel_oncall: go ahead. do a rolling restart and watch for cold-start latency. command to use:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker-42 -n runtime
```

mike_sre: restarting now. tailing logs. ETA ~2m.

mike_sre: restart succeeded. logs show worker reconnected to kvstore and cache warmed. latency improving in the next 60s.

evan_support: update to AcmeCorp: we’ve applied temporary rate limiting and restarted a backend worker; some requests may still show elevated latency as caches warm. ETA for full recovery ~30–60 min. Will follow up.

carla_customer_success: pinging AcmeCorp — they confirm partial recovery; still seeing occasional 503s. asking for example request ids.

anita_prod: can we switch AcmeCorp to a dedicated pool for the short term? their workload is bursty and heavy. that would isolate them while we investigate.

sara_platform: we can move them to a Dedicated pool, but needs approval from infra. provisioning a hot capacity slot (short-lived) now. request ID RED-1829.

ops-bot: Dedicated slot provisioned and routing rule applied for customer_acme (route tag: acme-dedicated). Traffic shifting gradually.

joel_oncall: traffic to shared pool dropped ~90% for acme, shared latency back to normal. Good win.

mike_sre: collecting logs for postmortem. saving snapshots of kvstore metrics, gateway traces, and sample payloads from offending requests (we have request ids). pushing artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/INF-482/

anita_prod: schedule postmortem? I can host. propose 1710060000 (one day out) 10:30am PT. agenda: timeline, root cause hypotheses, action items, customer impact review.

joel_oncall: works for me. please include infra, eng-sre, platform, and customer success. invite link: https://meet.redwood.ai/INF-482-postmortem

evan_support: I’ll prepare customer impact summary and list of affected keys/tenants. Will upload CSV to the doc.

carla_customer_success: I’ll draft the customer-facing incident note for AcmeCorp and other potentially affected customers. sending initial message now.

mike_sre: action items created in Jira:
- RED-1830: investigate kvstore timeouts and add circuit-breaker (owner: mike_sre)
- RED-1831: implement per-tenant connection caps on kvstore (owner: sara_platform)
- RED-1832: add alert for atypical seq_len distribution spikes (owner: joel_oncall)

joel_oncall: I’ll follow up on RED-1832 and owner handoff during the postmortem. Also adding runbook updates for restarting model-worker gracefully.

sara_platform: temporary mitigation idea — add a soft upstream validation that rejects absurdly large seq_len in single request (or chunk them). adding RFC draft to docs.

anita_prod: client communication plan: send initial summary within 2 hours, then detailed postmortem after internal review. assign to carla_customer_success and evan_support.

joel_oncall: on-call handoff note for next shift (cc @mike_sre): system currently stable, acme traffic on dedicated pool, ratelimits in place, tickets created. if kvstore timeouts reappear, escalate to eng-infra.

mike_sre: uploading logs and quick triage notes to the incident doc. marking which components to instrument more. linking to replay dashboards.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • INF-482 • status: MONITORING • severity downgraded to P2 after dedicated routing and restart. next check-in in 30m.

anita_prod: thanks everyone. please add any training topics to the postmortem doc — I want to propose a 45-min brown-bag next week on prevention patterns for high-throughput embedding pipelines.

sara_platform: I can present—outline: kvstore capacity planning, per-tenant limits, safe default model configs, and automated fallback patterns. will prepare slides and a short demo.

carla_customer_success: include a segment on how to spot and report problematic batched jobs from tenants; that helped us identify AcmeCorp load.

evan_support: adding notes about better escalation hooks and template language for customer updates. will post draft in #incidents-docs.

joel_oncall: final note: FILED: postmortem doc + meeting invite + assigned Jira tickets. I’ll run the postmortem and capture action owners. thanks all for the fast mitigation. :heart:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring) • INF-482 • closed at 1710003610 • summary uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/INF-482/summary.md"
